chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who travels in the month of Ramadan, does he break his fast at his home? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he resolves in his mind at night that he will travel, he breaks his fast when he leaves his home; and if he does not resolve it in his mind that night, but decides on it during the day while traveling, he completes his fast.'
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler's fast break if they decide to travel on the day of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the specific condition of 'intention' (niyyah) at dawn for travelers who remain in their homes, distinguishing between those who planned the journey the night before and those who decided during the day. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the timing of intention relative to the Fajr prayer, ensuring that the status of 'traveler' is established before the fast becomes obligatory for the day. It provides practical clarity for individuals whose travel plans are flexible, aligning with the broader principle that ease is granted in cases of genuine travel.
